'''Formats''' are the organized-play card pools and event types used for ''Star Wars'' CCG tournaments and casual games. Decipher-era play used printed cards under Decipher rules. After Decipher ended the game, the [[Players Committee]] added virtual cards and labeled constructed environments (notably '''Standard''' after the 2014 Virtual Card Reset, and '''Legacy''' for the pre-reset virtual pool).

Full format definitions, banned lists and event procedures are on [https://www.starwarsccg.org/ starwarsccg.org]<ref name="pc-home">[https://www.starwarsccg.org/ Star Wars Players Committee], starwarsccg.org. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261020234753/https://swccg.com/snapshots/pc/home.html Internet Archive].</ref> and in the PDFs linked below.<ref name="pc-tr">[https://www.starwarsccg.org/resources/tournament-resources/ Tournament resources], starwarsccg.org. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261021115728/https://swccg.com/snapshots/pc/tournament-resources.html Internet Archive].</ref><ref name="pc-rules">[https://www.starwarsccg.org/rules/ Rules], starwarsccg.org. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261021120438/https://swccg.com/snapshots/pc/rules.html Internet Archive].</ref>

Every format on the [[GEMP]] format list has its own page on this wiki. The sections below group them by era and family, with one line on each. The [[#GEMP environments|GEMP environments]] table at the end gives every GEMP name and code.<ref name="gemp">[https://github.com/billbisco/swccg-gemp/blob/16168b26aa0c245d4427f58bbb023338af3cbf6b/src/gemp-swccg-server/src/main/resources/swccgFormats.json swccgFormats.json], GEMP source code (billbisco/swccg-gemp, commit 16168b26), GitHub. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261021114513/https://swccg.com/snapshots/github/billbisco/swccg-gemp/ec48dc19/swccgFormats.json.html Internet Archive]. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261022040117/https://github.com/billbisco/swccg-gemp/blob/16168b26aa0c245d4427f58bbb023338af3cbf6b/src/gemp-swccg-server/src/main/resources/swccgFormats.json Internet Archive].</ref>

The Players Committee ''Alternate Format Tournament Guide'' (revised September 2015) describes two primary constructed pools after the Reset:<ref name="afg">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/wp/wp-content/uploads/Alternate-Formats-Guide.pdf Star Wars CCG Alternate Format Tournament Guide] (revised 09/2015), Players Committee. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008195355/https://res.starwarsccg.org/wp/wp-content/uploads/Alternate-Formats-Guide.pdf Internet Archive].</ref>

* '''Standard''' / [[Open]] &mdash; Decipher cards plus the post-2014 current Virtual Set cards (slanted-ring virtual set icon).
* '''[[Legacy Open|Legacy]]''' &mdash; Decipher cards plus Legacy Virtual Cards from before the Fall 2014 reset (black-diamond virtual block icon). The [[2014 World Championship]] was the last championship circuit to use that pool.<ref name="afg" />

Deck size and "outside the deck" cards (for example Defensive Shields under a Starting Effect) follow the tournament document in force for the event. See the Tournament Guide and [[Players Committee Advanced Rulebook]].

== Decipher-era constructed pools ==

Era hub: [[Decipher era]]. Decipher Worlds used the printed sets legal at the time, from [[Premiere]] through the newest expansion. [[Decipher deck designs]] used the same rule for the publication month. The complete print run is [[Premiere - Theed Palace]].

* [[Premiere (format)|Premiere]] — May–June 1996 Deck Designs
* [[Premiere - A New Hope]] — [[1996 Decipher World Championship]]; July–November 1996 Deck Designs
* [[Premiere - Hoth]] — early 1997 Deck Designs (through April)
* [[Premiere - Dagobah]] — mid 1997 Deck Designs; [[1997 Kiffex Regionals]]; [[1997 Sullust Regionals]]
* [[Premiere - Cloud City]] — [[1997 Decipher World Championship]]
** [[Premiere - Cloud City (Modified)]] — the same pool with a ban list, used in the [[Retro League]]
* [[Premiere - Jabba's Palace]] — 1998 Deck Designs (through October)
* [[Premiere - Special Edition]] — [[1998 Decipher World Championship]]
* [[Premiere - Endor]] — [[1999 Decipher World Championship]]
* [[Premiere - Death Star II]] — [[2000 Decipher World Championship]]; also [[2021 Retro Event (Premiere to Death Star II)]] and later GEMP Retro / Premiere-to-DSII events
** Also used for the [[2026 Retro GEMP Match Play Championship (Premiere to DSII)]]
* [[Premiere - Jabba's Palace Sealed Deck]] — Premiere through the [[Jabba's Palace Sealed Deck]] product (GEMP name '''Premiere - JPSD''')
* [[Premiere - Tatooine]] — [[2001 Brugge Belgian Open]]
* [[Premiere - Coruscant]] — printed Decipher through [[Coruscant (expansion)|Coruscant]]
* [[Premiere - Reflections II]] — [[2021 Worlds Throwback Event]] (Premiere through Reflections II)
** [[Premiere - Reflections II (Modified)]] — the same pool with a ban list
* [[Premiere - Reflections III]] — [[2001 Decipher World Championship]]
* [[Premiere - Theed Palace]] — complete Decipher print run; [[2022 Decipher Cards Only Retro Event]] (GEMP environment name '''Decipher Cards Only''')
** [[Decipher Cards Only (Modified)]] — the same pool with a ban list
* [[Episode I Closed Environment]] — Decipher's Episode I-icon-only constructed format (2001–2002; also called Type II); [[DecipherCon 2002]] Episode I ONLY event

== Virtual Original constructed (2002–2009) ==

Era hub: [[Virtual Original]]. From March 2002 until the September 2009 Block reorganization, championship constructed was printed Decipher cards plus the original numbered Virtual Sets that were legal on the event date. Each cutoff is its own format hub, titled '''Premiere - Original VS{N}''' (short redirect '''POVS{N}'''). Legal days live on [[Virtual Sets (2002-2009)]]. The complete Original pool is [[Premiere - Original VS17]] (redirect [[Original Virtual Open]]).

* [[Premiere - Original VS1]] (redirect [[POVS1]]) — printed Decipher through [[Theed Palace]] plus original Virtual Set 1. Legal 9 March 2002. Used on [[Game Players Network decks]] from that day.
* [[Premiere - Original VS2]] (redirect [[POVS2]]) — printed Decipher through [[Theed Palace]] plus original Virtual Sets 1–2. Legal 1 June 2002. Used on [[Greg Zinn Shes Virtually Back]].
* [[Premiere - Original VS3]] (redirect [[POVS3]]) — printed Decipher through [[Theed Palace]] plus original Virtual Sets 1–3. Used for the [[2002 World Championship]].
* [[Premiere - Original VS13]] (redirect [[POVS13]]) — printed Decipher through [[Theed Palace]] plus original Virtual Sets 1–13, including [[Virtual Set: Defensive Shields|Defensive Shields]]. Used for the [[2007 World Championship]].
* [[Premiere - Original VS16]] (redirect [[POVS16]]) — printed Decipher through [[Theed Palace]] plus original Virtual Sets 1–16, including [[Virtual Set: Defensive Shields|Defensive Shields]]. Used for the [[2008 World Championship]].
* [[Premiere - Original VS17]] (redirect [[POVS17]] / [[Original Virtual Open]]) — printed Decipher through [[Theed Palace]] plus original Virtual Sets 1–17, including Defensive Shields. Complete [[Virtual Original]] pool. Legal 6 February 2009.

== Virtual Legacy constructed (2009–2014) ==

Era hub: [[Virtual Legacy]]. Set index: [[Virtual Blocks (2009-2014)]]. After the 2009 Block reorganization, championship constructed used the pre-reset Virtual Block pool. The full pool is [[Legacy Open]]; the [[2014 World Championship]] was the last circuit event in that pool.

* [[Legacy Open]] (<code>legacy</code>) &mdash; Decipher cards plus pre-reset Virtual Block cards. Used for the [[2014 World Championship]].

== Virtual Modern constructed (2014–) ==

Era hub: [[Virtual Modern]]. Set index: [[Current Virtual Sets]]. The full current virtual pool and its GEMP variants.<ref name="gemp" /> Some later PC articles and events also say '''Open''' for constructed decks that include Virtual Cards and Shields.<ref name="wend-open">[https://www.starwarsccg.org/wends-world-thematic-deck-match-ups-series-1/ Wend's World - Thematic Deck Match-ups Series (#1)], starwarsccg.org. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261021115933/https://swccg.com/snapshots/pc/wends-world-thematic-deck-match-ups-series-1.html Internet Archive].</ref>

* [[Open]] &mdash; current virtual constructed environment (Decipher cards plus current Virtual Sets and Shields). Used for the [[2026 Tenth Annual GEMPC]].
* [[Open (40 cards)]] &mdash; the Open pool with 40-card decks.
* [[Open (45 cards)]] &mdash; the Open pool with 45-card decks.
* [[Open (100 cards)]] &mdash; the Open pool with 100-card decks and a 90-minute default timer; the Players Committee's 100 Card Deck Format.
* [[Open (no shields)]] &mdash; the Open pool without Defensive Shields.
* [[Open (no shields / no v-cards)]] &mdash; Decipher cards only, without Defensive Shields.
* [[Open (no Episode VII)]] &mdash; the Open pool without Episode VII icon cards.

== Current-virtual retro pools ==

These use '''current''' Virtual Set numbering, not 2002&ndash;2009 original slips.

* [[Premiere - Virtual Set 3]] (<code>premiere_set3</code>) &mdash; Decipher cards plus current Virtual Sets through Virtual Set 3. Distinct from [[Premiere - Original VS3]] (2002 original slips) and from [[Premiere to Virtual Set 3]] (the 2025 charity event that uses this current-virtual pool).
* [[Premiere to Virtual Set 3]] &mdash; the pool of the [[2025 Online Retro Event for Charity]].

== Classic family ==
Classic formats ban cards with the Episode I or Maintenance icon.<ref name="gemp" /><ref name="afg" />
* [[Classic]] &mdash; Decipher and current virtual cards, without Defensive Shield, Episode I or Maintenance icon cards.
* [[Classic (no v-cards)]] &mdash; Classic with Decipher cards only. Forum threads call it "Classic No-V".
* [[Classic (no v-cards) (Modified)]] &mdash; Classic (no v-cards) with 14 Defensive Shields allowed. Used in the [[Retro League]].
* [[Episode I Closed Environment]] &mdash; the opposite closed environment: only cards with the Episode I icon.<ref name="afg" />

Closed-environment and themed constructed variants, such as Classic, [[Episode I Closed Environment]], Battle of Endor Environment, team events and The Bith Shuffle, are defined in the Alternate Format Tournament Guide.<ref name="afg" />

== Other labeled formats ==

The Players Committee maintains additional constructed and casual formats under the '''SWCCG Formats''' menu on [https://www.starwarsccg.org/ starwarsccg.org].<ref name="pc-home" /> Full definitions, banned lists and version notes are on the PC pages cited on each format page.
* [[Jawa Format]] &mdash; a format that removes the top of the power curve with a ban list.<ref name="pc-jawa">[https://www.starwarsccg.org/jawa/ Jawa Format], starwarsccg.org. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261021120146/https://swccg.com/snapshots/pc/jawa.html Internet Archive].</ref>
* [[Scavenger Format]] &mdash; Decipher cards of common rarities only.<ref name="pc-scav">[https://www.starwarsccg.org/scavenger/ Scavenger Format], starwarsccg.org. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261021120256/https://swccg.com/snapshots/pc/scavenger.html Internet Archive].</ref>
* [[Ewok Format]] &mdash; ''Premiere - Death Star II (Ewok)'', the Premiere&ndash;Death Star II pool with a long ban list, created for the 2026 Retro Ewok Championship.
* [[Utinni! (Jawas Only)]] &mdash; characters are restricted to Jawas.<ref name="pc-utinni">[https://www.starwarsccg.org/utinni/ Utinni!], starwarsccg.org. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261021115114/https://swccg.com/snapshots/pc/utinni.html Internet Archive].</ref>
* [[Limited Resources Format]] &mdash; Decipher cards with the most abusive removed and some virtual cards added.
* [[Open (100 cards)]] &mdash; the 100 Card Deck Format.

== Limited / sealed and draft ==

Sealed and booster-draft events use unopened product (or a fixed cube pool) instead of a full constructed library. The guide lists product-specific sealed and draft variants: Premiere Sealed, Official Tournament Sealed Deck sealed/draft, Enhanced Premiere Pack Overdrive, Death Star II sealed/draft, Reflections booster draft and Secret Squirrel. It also defines '''Watto's Cube''', a fixed ~450-card draft pool.<ref name="afg" /> The Players Committee maintains the official cube list.<ref name="pc-cube">[https://www.starwarsccg.org/cube/ Watto's Chance Cube], starwarsccg.org. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261021115326/https://swccg.com/snapshots/pc/cube.html Internet Archive].</ref>

[[First Anthology Sealed]] is a Decipher-era sealed pool from the [[First Anthology]] box (May 1997). The [[1997 Decipher World Championship First Anthology Sealed]] consolation used signed First Anthology sets.<ref name="dec-sealed">[http://www.decipher.com/starwars/specialevents/current/97worldfinals/sealedsummary.html Report 10], Decipher. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19980223172645/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/specialevents/current/97worldfinals/sealedsummary.html Internet Archive]</ref>

GEMP limited formats all use 40-card decks.<ref name="gemp" />
* Cube and draft:

* GEMP products: [[GEMP sealed league products]] lists what each GEMP sealed league issues. [[GEMP draft and cube products]] lists the GEMP draft pools and how picks work.

== Casual and testing (GEMP) ==
* [[Anything Goes]] — intended default Casual and AI environment on this instance (constructed collection, all sets, 40–60 cards). Further work is listed on [[GEMP planned features]].
* [[Playtesting]] &mdash; the Open pool plus the Playtesting set.
* [[Dream Cards]] &mdash; the Open pool plus the Dream Cards set.

=== Differences from the Players Committee GEMP ===
The format list on play.swccg.com (billbisco/swccg-gemp, commit 16168b26) has 51 formats. The Players Committee format list (PlayersCommittee/gemp-swccg-public, commit 5e26dd19) has 37.<ref name="gemp" /><ref name="pc-gemp">[https://github.com/PlayersCommittee/gemp-swccg-public/blob/5e26dd19cc700adbf77de53e0d7b89720c94f03e/src/gemp-swccg-server/src/main/resources/swccgFormats.json swccgFormats.json], GEMP source code (PlayersCommittee/gemp-swccg-public, commit 5e26dd19), GitHub. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261021130403/https://swccg.com/snapshots/github/PlayersCommittee/gemp-swccg-public/5e26dd19/swccgFormats.json.html Internet Archive].</ref> The differences are:
* Formats only on play.swccg.com: [[Anything Goes]], [[Ewok Format|Ewok]], [[Premiere - A New Hope Sealed]], [[Endor - Death Star II Sealed]], [[Reflections Sealed]], [[Episode I Sealed]], [[All Of The Jedi Sealed]], [[Novelty - Space Sealed]], [[Watto's Cube with objective packs Cube]], [[Watto's Cube with fixed pack Cube]], [[Premiere - Death Star II Draft]], [[Premiere - Virtual Set 13 Draft]], [[Premiere - Virtual Set 25 Draft]] and [[Cube v7 + Objectives Draft]].<ref name="gemp" /><ref name="pc-gemp" />
* [[Cube]]: 40 cards on play.swccg.com and 45 cards in the Players Committee code.<ref name="gemp" /><ref name="pc-gemp" />
* [[Jabba's Palace Sealed]] (<code>jp_sealed</code>): named "Jabba's Palace Sealed" on play.swccg.com and "JP Sealed" in the Players Committee code.<ref name="gemp" /><ref name="pc-gemp" />
* [[Legacy Open|Legacy]]: play.swccg.com adds 18 set numbers from 1200 to 1292 and the <code>loreHeroicRule</code> setting.<ref name="gemp" /><ref name="pc-gemp" />
Differences in sealed league products and draft files are listed at [[GEMP sealed league products#Differences from the Players Committee GEMP|GEMP sealed league products]] and [[GEMP draft and cube products#Differences from the Players Committee GEMP|GEMP draft and cube products]].
